findings.claim: "When answering a Describe Two Features question ... give two distinct features with supporting detail" — presented as a named 4-mark form.
findings.truth: 'Describe two features' for 4 marks belongs to another board. In this section the describe question is worth 2 marks.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/history-a-J410.md non-British depth study assessment tables

findings.claim: "Historians including Roderick MacFarquhar estimate that mass campaigns and land reform together resulted in between one and three million executions"; flashcard answer "Frank Dikötter (or Roderick MacFarquhar)".
findings.truth: MacFarquhar's work is on the origins and course of the Cultural Revolution, not on land-reform death tolls. The 1–3 million range for the early campaigns comes from Dikötter and others working on 1949–57. Attribution generalised; flashcard keeps Dikötter.
findings.evidence: Frank Dikötter, The Tragedy of Liberation (1945–57); MacFarquhar, Origins of the Cultural Revolution

findings.claim: Gao Gang "was expelled from the Party in 1954".
findings.truth: Gao Gang was denounced and removed from power in February 1954 and died in August 1954; formal expulsion followed at the national Party conference in March 1955. 'Purged in 1954' is fair at GCSE, so no edit made.
findings.evidence: standard accounts of the Gao Gang–Rao Shushi affair

findings.claim: "The All-China Women's Federation, expanded from 1956 ..." and "expanded significantly from 1956 under the leadership of Deng Yingchao".
findings.truth: The Federation was founded on 24 March 1949 (renamed in 1957) and was chaired from 1949 by Cai Chang. Deng Yingchao was a vice-chair, not its leader.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'All-China Women's Federation' — founded 24 March 1949, first chair Cai Chang

findings.claim: Dazhai is presented as a Great Leap Forward model, with the slogan "promoted across China through the 1960s and 1970s".
findings.truth: Dazhai became the national model after the Great Leap: Mao issued 'In Agriculture, Learn from Dazhai' in 1964. The lesson now dates the slogan.
findings.evidence: standard chronology of the Dazhai model campaign; spec lists Dazhai under both key topic 1 and key topic 2

findings.claim: "In September 1966, the Destroy the Four Olds Campaign was launched."
findings.truth: The campaign began in Beijing on 19 August 1966, during 'Red August'.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Four Olds' — campaign began August 1966 (19 August in Beijing)

findings.claim: The Central Cultural Revolution Group described as "led by Jiang Qing".
findings.truth: Chen Boda headed the group; Jiang Qing was first deputy head and dominated cultural policy. 'Dominated by' would be exact, but the point is not examined at GCSE, so no edit made.
findings.evidence: membership of the Central Cultural Revolution Group, 1966

findings.claim: "Universities were closed from 1966 and did not fully reopen until 1977."
findings.truth: Universities began taking worker-peasant-soldier students again from about 1970; what returned in 1977 was entry by examination. The word 'fully' keeps the sentence defensible, so no edit made.
findings.evidence: restoration of the gaokao in 1977, covered in lesson 9

findings.claim: "Examiners reward students who present contested topics with appropriate nuance."
findings.truth: An invented claim about examiner behaviour. Replaced with advice about the answer itself.
findings.evidence: no such statement in specs/ocr/history-a-J410.md

findings.claim: "Red Guards destroyed hundreds of Tibetan monasteries."
findings.truth: Tibetan exile sources put the number destroyed across 1959–76 in the thousands (about 6,000); the PRC disputes it. The scale is genuinely contested and the lesson already says so, so no figure was substituted.
findings.evidence: contested figures; no settled value found

findings.claim: Hua Guofeng "was outmanoeuvred by Deng Xiaoping by 1978 and resigned in 1980" — while the same lesson, its glossary and a flashcard all say 1981.
findings.truth: Hua resigned as Premier in September 1980 and as Party Chairman in June 1981. The lesson's own narrative and flashcards use 1981, so the definition now specifies Party Chairman in 1981.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction within the lesson; standard chronology

findings.claim: "Deng coined the concept of socialism with Chinese characteristics", placed alongside 1979–81 events.
findings.truth: Deng used the phrase at the Twelfth Party Congress in September 1982, just outside this option's 1981 end date. It works here as framing rather than as a dated event, so no edit made.
findings.evidence: spec period is 1950–1981

findings.claim: The 1980 Marriage Law "introduced explicit protections against domestic violence" — repeated in the glossary, a flashcard and a knowledge-check stem.
findings.truth: The 1980 law raised the legal age of marriage to 22 for men and 20 for women, made family planning a duty of both spouses (tying it to the One Child Policy) and allowed divorce on breakdown of affection. An explicit ban on domestic violence was added by the 2001 amendment.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China' — 1980 revision raised ages to 20/22 and bolstered the one-child policy

findings.claim: "rural families in many provinces were permitted a second child if the first was a girl", given as a feature of the policy in this period.
findings.truth: The daughter-only exception was opened by central document in 1984, after the 1981 end of this option. Now dated.
findings.evidence: standard chronology of One Child Policy relaxations

findings.claim: "In 1981, compulsory primary education was further extended to ensure broader access at the foundation level", with a flashcard drilling 1981 as the answer.
findings.truth: No settled event matches 1981. The Party and State Council decision on universalising primary education was December 1980; compulsory education was written into the 1982 constitution and into law in 1986. Options: (a) strike the sentence and repoint the flashcard to another fact in the lesson; (b) redate it to the December 1980 decision. Recommendation: (a) — the claim is unverifiable and the flashcard makes students memorise it.
findings.evidence: no supporting source found; 1986 Compulsory Education Law is the settled milestone and sits outside the period
findings.ruling: Redated to the December 1980 decision; flashcard repointed.

summary: Every lesson labelled its practice questions with question forms and marks from other boards (4, 8, 16 and 24-mark questions); all nine sets were relabelled to the genuine 2 / 10 / 18-mark forms. Content errors were few but real: the All-China Women's Federation's founding date and leader, the month the Four Olds campaign began, the date of the Dazhai model, Hua Guofeng's resignation year, and a domestic-violence provision the 1980 Marriage Law did not contain.
